title: CUTOVER journal: an unguarded rollback affordance that decays

completion_criteria.text: What CUTOVER's sha field means is settled against the design intent rather than inferred from code alone: the cutover event's release, or a claim about which release is currently live.
The inherited 'CUTOVER is WRONG' framing is confirmed or corrected on evidence, since the journal may be an accurate record of the one cutover actually performed.
cutover.mjs rollback refuses, or demands an explicit override, when its asides no longer correspond to live state - proven by a test red before the guard and green after.
applyCutover's silent carry-forward of a stale journal through mergeJournal is either guarded on the same liveness test or explicitly accepted with a stated reason.
The retained-affordance lifecycle is decided: a journal either expires once a later promotion supersedes it, or is retained deliberately with the decay hazard documented.
Whether node scripts/config/cutover.mjs rollback is caught by the bash gate is answered by running the gate's own decision function on that command, checked against its threat model.

key_decisions.title: The CUTOVER defect is an unguarded restore path, not a wrong value in a file
